title: The Classic of Tea (English)
summary: A complete English reading of the Chajing, written by Lu Yu in the eighth century — the first book ever written about tea. Three scrolls and ten chapters: the plant, the tools, the making, the twenty-four vessels, the boiling, the drinking, the whole written record of tea before the Tang, the tea districts of the empire, what may be left out in the open air, and the scroll to hang beside your seat. Every paragraph is translated, including Lu Yu's own interlinear notes. Collated against the Siku quanshu text and read leaf by leaf against a Ming printing of the Baichuan xuehai, the earliest surviving line of the text.
